newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues tough rules on urban re-employment.
newsitem.headline: China issues tough rules on urban re-employment.

text.p: China has asked local officials to boost their efforts on resettlement of laid-off workers and guarantee their basic living standard, official media said on Wednesday.

The Ministry of Labour, along with other government departments, has jointly issued a directive ordering municipal officials to create new jobs for more than 50 percent of local jobless workers, the China Economic Times said.
The rules apply to China's pilot cities chosen for implementing bankruptcies, it said. The government has expanded the number of pilot cities to 110 this year from 58 previously.
Officials should take measures to prevent workers' income from falling short of the minimum living standard set by each municipal government, the newspaper said.

China has set monthly minimum income levels for its urban residents in more than 100 cities at between 96 yuan ($12) and 170 yuan ($20). Those whose income falls short of the minimum living standard would be eligible for municipal relief funds.
Many of China's state enterprises are losing money and have been trying to cut their bloated payrolls to increase efficiency and compete in the marketplace.
